Additional Solicitor General, was requested to obtain a
medical report from the All India Institute of Medical
Sciences, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as "AIIMS").
6. The matter was listed on 24.07.2026. The petitioner
was subjected to medical examination and a medical report
has also been filed in the matter and the conclusion of the
Medical Board which is comprising of six senior doctors
reads as under:
“Conclusion
In view of the clinical assessment and the
available medical records, the Medical Board
is of the opinion that the petitioner is
clinically stable at present. He has been
advised  to  continue  medical  management,

present. However, in the medical report it has been advised

1. Heard Mr. S. Nagamuthu, learned Senior Counsel for

2. The  present  petition  calls  in  question  the
correctness  of  the  order  dated  27-02-2026  in  CRM
No.86916/2025 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Patna. By the said order, the petitioner has been
denied the benefit of bail in connection with FIR
No.1435/2023 registered with Danapur Police Station,
District Patna, Bihar,  for the offences punishable
under Sections 147, 148, 149, 341, 323, 307 & 504 of
the Indian Penal Code, 1860(for short, ‘IPC’), later
Section 302 of IPC also added and under Section 27 of
the Arms Act, 1959.
3.  On 14.07.2026, this Court wanted to counsel for the
State to obtain instructions on the cross case bearing
CC No.1605/2023 instituted by the petitioner’s mother.
Learned counsel for the State today reports that CC
No.1605/2023 is indeed a cross case and that is at the
stage of cognizance, with cognizance not yet taken.
4. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submits
that being a cross case, under law it will have to be
tried with the case instituted against the petitioner
by the same Court and judgment delivered on the same

--- Page 221 ---
3
date.  Learned  Senior  Counsel  submits  that  the
petitioner had already undergone about two years and
seven months in custody. Learned Senior Counsel also
draws attention to the counter affidavit of the State
wherein in paragraph 6, dealing with the Forensic
Science Laboratory report (for short, ‘FSL report’), it
is recorded that the FSL report is not conclusive with
regard to the weapon of offence and as to whether the
weapon discovered at the behest of the petitioner, was
the weapon used in the offence.
5. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of
the case, we are inclined to enlarge the petitioner on
bail.
6. Accordingly, we direct that petitioner shall be
enlarged on bail subject to the satisfaction of the
concerned Trial Court in connection with the aforesaid
FIR and for the offences mentioned hereinabove.
7. Needless to say that the observations in this order
are  only  for  the  purpose  of  deciding  the  bail
application/prayer of the petitioner. The trial in
another  proceedings  will  proceed  independently  in
accordance with law on its own merits uninfluenced by
any of the observations in the order.
8. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the
above terms.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.10018/2016
BHARAT SANCHAR NIGAM L TD. 
THR ITS CMD. & ORS.              APPELLANTS
VERSUS
PRAMOD KUMAR DIXIT    RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. A laconic order of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Bench at
Lucknow)1 dated 23 rd May, 2016 is under challenge in this appeal by special
leave granted on 3rd October, 2016.
2. Major portion of the impugned order, spread over three pages, reproduces
the order of the Central Administrative Tribunal2, Lucknow dated 11th December,
2015,  allowing  the  original  application  of  the  respondent  and,  thereafter,
concludes in one line:
"We have gone through the finding recorded by the Tribunal and we do
not find any illegality in the same."
3. We do not approve of the manner in which the Division Bench disposed of
the writ petition instituted by the appellants. In the ordinary course, a remand
could have been ordered but having regard to the fact that much water has
flown  under  the  bridge  and  the  respondent  is  now  a  septuagenarian,  we
proceed to consider the challenge on its own merits.
1 High Court
2 Tribunal
1

--- Page 224 ---
4. Respondent was recommended for promotion as Senior Accounts Officer 3
by the  Departmental Promotion  Committee4 on  1st January,  2001. However,
owing to pending disciplinary proceedings, the recommendation was not acted
upon.
5. Such disciplinary proceedings culminated in an order of punishment of
withholding of increments for two years without cumulative effect. Since the
respondent was visited with an order of penalty, the appellants did not promote
him. Action of the appellants in not promoting the respondent was the subject
matter of challenge before the T ribunal.
6. The Tribunal came to a curious finding that since the period for which the
penalty was to remain operative had lapsed, the right of the respondent to
obtain  promotion  revived.  Accordingly,  directions  were  issued  requiring  the
appellants  to  promote  the  respondent  to  the  post  of  SAO  based  on  the
recommendations of the DPC.
7. It is this order of the T ribunal in which the Division Bench did not find any
illegality. We are afraid, the order of the Tribunal is absolutely indefensible and
should not have been sustained by the High Court.
8. Effect of the order of punishment of stoppage of increments was that for a
period  of  two  years,  the  respondent  would  not  be  entitled  to  increments;
however,  after  expiry  of  such  period,  he  would  again  become  entitled  to
increments. However, what is of significance is that such penalty operated as a
bar to the respondent’s promotion as SAO and, if we may say, rightly so. As a
general rule, an officer subjected to penalty in disciplinary proceedings is not
promoted. The right to be considered for promotion revives only after the period
of penalty ends. Appellants, by not promoting the respondent to the post of
3 SAO
4 DPC
2

--- Page 225 ---
SAO, did not commit any illegality warranting interference.
9. In such view of the matter, the appeal succeeds. The impugned order of
the High Court as well as that of the T ribunal is set aside with the result that the
original application filed before the T ribunal shall stand dismissed.
10. Respondent shall, however, be entitled to terminal benefits as per law.
11. The civil appeal is, accordingly, allowed.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
..........................................J.
(DIPANKAR DATTA)
..........................................J.
(SHEEL NAGU)
New Delhi;
July 29, 2026.

  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO. 4743/2016
SMT. PINKI SHARAN       APPELLANT 
VERSUS
STATE OF JHARKHAND THROUGH ITS HOME 
SECRETARY & ORS.                            RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
1. This  appeal,  by  special  leave,  questions  the
impugned judgment and order dated 23 rd April, 20151 of the
High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi allowing an intra-court
appeal2 of the respondents.
2. Appellant,  upon  the  death  of  her  husband  in-
harness, was  appointed  on compassionate  ground  on the
post of a primary school teacher on 11th of August, 2012.
3. However, the appellant did not possess the Teacher
Eligibility  Test  (TET)  qualification,  which  is  an  essential
qualification  in  terms  of  the  provisions  of  the  Right  of
1  impugned judgment
2  LPA No.210 of 2014
1

--- Page 240 ---
Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 3. Her
appointment,  as  a  primary school  teacher, was  cancelled
and  vide proceedings  dated  18 th February,  2013  of  the
District  Education  Establishment  Committee,  she  was
recommended for appointment as a clerk in the Collectorate
against a vacant post.
4. The  crestfallen  appellant,  instead  of  accepting
appointment  as  a  clerk,  challenged  cancellation  of  her
appointment  in  the  writ  jurisdiction  of  the  High  Court  by
instituting a petition4.
5. Though  the  appellant  succeeded  before  the  writ
court, the Division Bench has reversed the decision and, in
our opinion, rightly.
6. The provisions of the RTE Act recently came up for
interpretation before this Court. In its decision in Anjuman
Ishaat-e-Taleem Trust v. State of Maharashtra 5 and, in
review from such decision, in State of U.P. Vs. Anjuman
Ishaat-E-Taleem  Trust  &  Ors. 6,  possession  of  TET
qualification  has  been  held  to  be  mandatory  for  those
aspiring for appointment as teachers in schools imparting
education  to  children  up  to  14  years  of  age  in  terms  of
Section 23 of the RTE Act.
3  RTE Act
4  WP(S) No.1897 of 2013
5  2025 SCC OnLine SC 1912
6  2026 INSC 597
2

--- Page 241 ---
7. Since,  the  appellant  has  not  acquired  the  TET
qualification till this date, she cannot have any valid claim to
the post of primary school teacher.
8. We find no reason to interfere with the impugned
judgment. The appeal is, accordingly, dismissed.
9. A  parting  observation  needs  to  be  made,  having
regard to the fact that it is after all a case of compassionate
appointment. In the event the appellant is willing to secure
employment as a clerk, she shall be at liberty to make a
representation to the State of Jharkhand; and, if there is a
vacancy where she can still be accommodated, her prayer
may be considered in the light of the resolution dated 13 th
May, 2013.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
…..…………………………………….J
(DIPANKAR DATTA)
………………………………………….J
(SHEEL NAGU)
NEW DELHI; 
JULY 28, 2026.

ORDER
1. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Haryana.
2. Leave granted.
3. Appellant is aggrieved by order dated 23.02.2026
passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana (briefly
the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the regular
bail application of the appellant.
4. Appellant  is  an  accused  in  FIR  No.211/2025
registered  at  Police  Station-  Panchkula,  District-
Panchkula under Sections 318(4), 336(2), 336(3), 338,
340 and 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for
short, ‘BNS’).
5. As per the FIR, the informant, who is a retired
police officer of the United Kingdom, and who wanted to
1

--- Page 244 ---
purchase land at Haryana, was duped by the accused
persons presenting themselves as owner of a plot of
land by forging a Will and related documents.
6. This Court, vide order dated 25.05.2026, had issued
notice, pursuant to which respondent-State of Haryana
has filed counter affidavit.
7. From Paragraph No.10 of the counter affidavit, it
is  seen  that  investigation  is  complete,  whereafter
charge  sheet  has  been  submitted  before  the  Court.
However,  investigation  as  against  co-accused  Puneet
Kumar and Harpreet Singh @ Happy is not complete as
they are absconding.
8. We find that appellant is a Typist, who had typed
out the Will in question. He has been in custody since
07.10.2025.  Charges  against  the  appellant  is  a
Magistrate  triable  one.  In  view  thereof,  we  are
inclined to grant bail to the appellant.
9. Accordingly, t he impugned order dated 23.02.2026,
qua the appellant, passed by the High Court is set
aside.
10. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced  before  the  concerned  Judicial  Magistrate
within  a  maximum  period  of  07  days  from  today,
whereafter he shall be released on bail on such terms
and conditions as may be deemed appropriate.
2

--- Page 245 ---

12. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

Station- Peddapuram, District- Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh
under  Sections  80(1)/3(5)  of  the  Bharatiya  Nyaya

6. The allegation against the appellant(s) in the FIR
lodged by the mother of the deceased is that the
daughter-in-law was subjected to illegal dowry demand
and on her failure to pay the same, she was subjected
to both physical and mental abuse by her husband.
7. This Court, by order dated 24.04.2026, had issued
notice  and  granted  interim  protection  to  the
appellant(s) subject to the appellant(s) co-operating
with the investigation.
8. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that
there are no direct allegation or overt act attributed
to the appellants.
9. On a query by the Court, learned counsel for the
respondent-State  of  Andhra  Pradesh  submits  that
appellant(s) have co-operated with the investigation.
She also submits that the husband of the deceased has
been granted regular bail.
10. Considering the above, we are of the view that the
interim protection granted by this Court vide order
dated 24.04.2026 should be made absolute.
11. That being the position, we set aside the impugned
order dated 22.01.2026 passed by the High Court and
make the order dated 24.04.2026 absolute. However, the

respondent-State  of  Chhattisgarh  seeks  time  to  file
counter affidavit, we are not inclined to grant further
time to her considering the nature of allegation and the
incarceration of the appellant.
4. Appellant is aggrieved by order dated 07.04.2026
passed by the High Court of Chhattisgarh (briefly the
‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the regular bail
application of the appellant.
5. Appellant  is  an  accused  in  Crime  No.786/2025
registered at Police Station- Kotwali, District- Korba,
Chhattisgarh  under  Sections  64(2)(m)  and  69  of  the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short, ‘BNS’) read with
1

--- Page 256 ---
Sections 67 and 67(b) of the Information Technology Act,
2000 and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from
Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short, 'POCSO Act').
6. The prosecution case is that on 25.10.2025, the
mother of the victim lodged the related FIR against the
appellant alleging that there is a video of her daughter
being circulated on Instagram through the I.D. of the
appellant.  The  said  video  shows  the  victim  in  an
inappropriate condition.
7. The appellant was arrested on 25.10.2025 and since
then, he has been in custody.
8. This Court, vide order dated 09.06.2026, had issued
notice.
9. Learned  counsel  for  the  appellant  submits  that
appellant, who is a 21 year old youngster and the alleged
victim girl, who would be about 16-17 years old, are in a
consensual relationship. The alleged video has not been
retrieved from the phone of the appellant. Considering the
age of the appellant and the consensual nature of the
relationship, this Court may enlarge the appellant on
bail.
10. Learned  counsel  for  the  respondent-State  of
Chhattisgarh, however strongly opposes the prayer for
bail. She submits that the offending video was circulated
on Instagram through the appellant's I.D. The victim is a
minor girl and, therefore, provisions of POCSO Act would
be applicable.
2

--- Page 257 ---
11. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on
due  consideration,  particularly  having  regard  to  the
statement of the victim girl, we are inclined to release
the appellant on bail. While the alleged victim girl has
not opposed the enlargement of the appellant on bail, it
is her mother who is objecting to the grant of bail to the
appellant.  The  reasons  are  understandable.  Both  the
parties are in an impressionable age.
12. Having regard to the above,  the impugned order dated
07.04.2026 passed by the High Court is set aside.
13. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the concerned Magistrate within a maximum
period of 07 days from today, whereafter he shall be
released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be
deemed appropriate.
14. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
15. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

MANISH KUMAR                                       Appellant(s)

1. Leave granted.
2. Heard  learned  counsel  for  the
parties.
3. This  appeal  arises  from  an  order
dated 16.04.2026 passed by the High Court of
Delhi at New Delhi rejecting the regular
bail prayer of the appellant in connection
with FIR No. 120/2025, registered at P.S.
Special Cell, Delhi.  
4. The  submission  on  behalf  of  the
appellant is that the appellant is charged
with offences which are all triable by a
1

--- Page 268 ---
Court  of  Magistrate;  investigation  is
complete; charge-sheet has been submitted;
he has suffered incarceration for a period
exceeding seven months; and there is no
likelihood of trial being concluded in near
future. It has also been submitted that he
has no previous criminal antecedents.
5. The  learned  Counsel  for  the  State-
respondent has opposed the prayer for bail
by  highlighting  that  this  is  a  case
involving fraud of over 40 crores.
6. Be that as it may, we notice that
several other co-accused have been granted
bail.
7. Having  regard  to  the  nature  of
offences as also the period of incarceration
suffered pending trial, we are of the view
that  the  appellant  is  entitled  to  be
released on bail during trial. 
2

--- Page 269 ---
8. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. The
order passed by the High Court rejecting the
regular bail prayer of the appellant is set
aside.
9. The appellant shall be released on
bail on such terms and conditions as the
trial court may deem fit to impose in the
facts and circumstances of the case.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall
stand disposed of.

Leave granted.
It is not in dispute that the award inter se the
parties has become final.  However, the High Court,
whilst  confirming  the  award  vide  Order  dated
01.12.2021, has directed the Reference Court to keep
80% of the compensation amount deposited by the
respondent(s) herein, in an unencumberable and non-
pledgeable long term fixed deposit of 10 years at the
minimum in the name of the appellant(s), and to pay
the remaining 20% via deposit in their savings bank
account.  In  an  application  filed  by  the
appellants(s),  seeking  relaxation  of  the  said
conditions,  the  High  Court  vide  order  dated
06.04.2023 has modified the same to 60% and 40% to be
kept in the fixed deposit and the savings bank
deposit respectively.  

--- Page 272 ---
2
As the said amount is the amount due to the
appellant(s), the exercise undertaken by the High
Court is totally unwarranted.
In such view of the matter, the directions
issued by the High Court vide orders dated 01.12.2021
and 06.04.2023, stand set aside. 
Learned counsel appearing for the respondent(s)
submits that the order of the High Court has been
complied with.  In such view of the matter, the
appellant(s) is permitted to withdraw the amount so
deposited, both in the fixed deposit and in the
savings  bank  account,  without  prejudice  to  the
contentions of the parties.
In the event of any dispute, the same can be
worked out in the execution proceedings.
The appeal stands allowed, accordingly.
Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.           OF 2026
(@SLP(CRL.) NO.10967 OF 2026)
KRISHAN CHANDER MALIK ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
SIDHESHWAR SINGH @ SIDHESHWAR DALAL  ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. Since no orders adverse to the interest of the respondent is
being passed while disposing of this appeal as the present appeal,
if kept pending, the appellant, who is an accused and convicted
under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (NI Act)
would  protract  the  proceedings  and  thwart  the  same,  we  are
disposing of this appeal.
4. The appellant/accused, filed an appeal against an order of
conviction and sentence of one year simple imprisonment along with
fine of Rs.3,51,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 138
of NI Act, sought for production of additional evidence in the
appeal. Since the said application was rejected by the Appellate
Court, appellant filed a revision petition before the High Court,
wherein the interim stay of the proceedings before the Appellate
Court, was sought for, was not granted. Revision petition was
filed. No notice has been issued in the revision petition and the
High Court has also directed the Sessions Court not to adjourn the
matter simply because of the pendency of the present petition.
1

--- Page 296 ---
Essentially no fault can be laid at the doors of the High Court. Be
that as it may, fact remains no orders have been passed in the
revision petition. Hence, this appeal.
5. The said order of adjourning the matter having been challenged,
this Court by order dated 04.06.2026 directed the appellant to
deposit a sum of Rs.2 lakhs in the Registry of this Court and said
amount was ordered to be kept in a Fixed Deposit in a nationalised
bank initially for a period of three months and directed the
Registry to keep the FD alive by renewing, if required. In the
meanwhile, the further proceedings of the Appellate Court has been
stayed.
6. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and
on perusal of the records, we notice from the office report that
amount as ordered, has been deposited and the same has been kept in
a short term Fixed Deposit by the Registry.
7.The issue relating to rejection of application for additional
evidence, has to be adjudicated by the High Court. We are of the
view that the ends of justice would be met if the stay of the
proceedings before the Sessions Court, as ordered by this Court, is
continued till disposal of the revision petition and accordingly,
it is made absolute. We request the High Court to expeditiously
dispose of the revision petition as it stands on a very limited
issue, expeditiously and preferably within six weeks from today.
8. The amount in deposit along with accrued interest, shall be
transmitted by the Registry of the Court of Additional Sessions
Judge, Rohtak, forthwith and the Sessions Judge on receipt of the
orders, that would be passed in the revision petition by the
jurisdictional  High  Court,  Sessions  Court  shall  proceed  to
adjudicate the appeal on merits expeditiously and dispose of the
same within an outer limit of two months from the date of receipt
of the order from the High Court. The amount which is transmitted
2

--- Page 297 ---
to the Sessions Court, shall be paid to the successful party and
the Appellate Court would be at liberty to pass necessary orders in
that regard.
9. It is made clear that no prayer for adjournment shall be
entertained by the Sessions Court or the High Court, as the case
may be, and in the event of such a request being made, the advocate
can be discharged and an amicus curiae can be appointed from the
jurisdictional Bar or a panel counsel from the legal services
authority so as to conclude the proceedings as ordered hereinabove.
10. We also make it clear that without being influenced by any
observations made under the impugned order including this order,
the Courts below shall dispose of the matters on merits and in
accordance with law. Both Courts would be at liberty to mulct the
parties with costs as it deems fit on the principle of ‘cause
should follow cause’.
11. We hope and trust that both parties and their respective
learned counsels would extend full cooperation with the courts in
disposing the matter(s) and would not take any steps to delay or
protract the proceedings. Accordingly, the appeal stands disposed
of.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
..................J.
(ARAVIND KUMAR)

(VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)

      IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
TRANSFER PETITION   (Civil) No. 3409 OF 2024  
ARTI FAUJDAR PETITIONER
VERSUS
 INDERPAL    RESPONDENT
O R D E R
       1. Read the office report dated 15th July, 2026.
2. Mediation report has been received from the Mediation Centre, 
Rajasthan High Court, Jodhpur. As per the mediation report, mediation 
between the parties has failed to bring about any settlement.
3. The  marriage  between  the  petitioner-Arti  Faujdar  and  the
respondent-Inderpal, was solemnized on 10 th December, 2017. One
son was born to the petitioner and the respondent from the wedlock
on 14.12.2020. However, the parties have since drifted apart owing to
differences arising by and between them.
4. The respondent has instituted proceedings under Section 13 of
the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 titled “ Inderpal Vs. Arti Faujdar ” in the
Family Court, Palwal, Haryana.
5. On the multiple grounds urged in the petition, the petitioner has
sought for transfer of the aforesaid proceedings to the Family Court,

--- Page 312 ---
2
Jodhpur, Rajasthan.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
7. We  are  satisfied,  having  regard  to  the  inconvenience  the
petitioner is likely to face if the proceedings were continued before
the  Family Court, Palwal , Haryana  which is at a distance of around
612 kms from her present place of residence,  that interest of justice
demands grant of the prayer for transfer.
8. Hence,  the  transfer  petition  is  allowed.  Petition  No.  HMA
637/2023 titled “ Inderpal Vs. Arti Faujdar ” pending before the  Family
Court, Palwal, Haryana  is transferred to the  Family Court, Jodhpur,
Rajasthan. Records of Petition No. HMA 637/2023 be transferred to
the transferee court immediately.
9. To avoid delay, the parties are directed to appear before the
transferee court on 19th August, 2026. If any or both the parties fail to
appear on that day, the presiding officer of the transferee court will
fix  another  date  of  appearance.  Thereafter,  he  shall  be  free  to
proceed in accordance with law.
10.  The  presiding  officer  shall  endeavour  to  bring  about  a
settlement between the parties through the process of mediation,
notwithstanding the fact that mediation has failed. If the process is
unsuccessful once again, nothing shall preclude the presiding officer
to take the proceedings to its logical conclusion on its merits and in
accordance with law.
11. If the respondent is unable to attend the proceedings in person
on  any  occasion, he  will be at  liberty  to seek  permission to  attend

--- Page 313 ---
3
through the virtual mode and if such a permission is sought, the
presiding officer of the court may proceed to consider it reasonably.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

(DIPANKAR DATTA)
.............................J.
(SHEEL NAGU)
New Delhi;

                             O R D E R
1. In pursuance of our order dated 13 th October 2025, the Kolkata  
Municipal Corporation has filed an affidavit duly affirmed by an  
Assistant Engineer (Civil) Building Department Borough-IV 4 stating  
as under:

--- Page 320 ---
“ K. It is stated that the subject premises, namely  
Premises No. 258, Vivekananda Road, Ward No. 028,  
Borough  IV,  Kolkata-700006,  was  granted  building  
permission under Section 393A of the Kolkata Municipal  
Corporation Act, 1980 by the competent authority, upon  
thorough scrutiny of the submitted drawings, designs,  
structural documents and other statutory requirements.  
There has been no fraudulent permission obtained by the 
applicant/developer  nor  any  improper  relaxation  or 
deviation allowed by KMC in the matter of sanction.
L. It is stated that the average road width of access  
at the location of the subject premises is 30.48 meters 
(100 feet), as recorded by the KMC Survey Department  
and reflected in the sanctioned building plans and key  
plan forming part of the approval record. The width  
satisfies  all  mandatory  requirements  under  the  
prevailing KMC Building Rules. The said sanctioned plan 
also  clearly  delineates  the  road  alignment,  the  
surrounding structures and the existing right-of-way.
M. It is stated that the Total Floor Area Ratio (FAR)  
sanctioned in respect of the subject project is 2.566,  
which is within the permissible threshold prescribed  
for this category and zone as total width of service  
road is 6.5 m and total road width including service  
road and Bagmari Bridge is 30.48m. The total height of  
the building and structural configuration are strictly  
within the limits allowed under applicable Kolkata  
Municipal Building Rules, 2009 and no part of the  
construction violates the sanctioned granted by the  
Corporation.
N.  It  is  further  submitted  that  field-  level  
inspections have been carried out repeatedly by KMC  
Officers including when petition was pending in High  
Court  and  report  have  been  submitted  accordingly. 
Complaints alleging violations were examined but were  
found to be factually incorrect.
O.  Further,  regarding  the  allegation  that  the  
construction  may  adversely  affect  the  structural  
integrity  or  safety  of  Bagmari  Bridge  and  its  
approaches, it is most respectfully submitted that a  
comprehensive pressure-bulb assessment for the proposed 
building (B+G+VI) has been independently conducted by  
the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA),  
Roads & Bridges Sector. Upon detailed analysis the  

--- Page 321 ---
Department has conclusively opined that the pressure  
exerted from the proposed structure upon the bridge  
approach  walls  will  be  negligible  and  no  harmful 
effects on the integrity or safety of the bridge  
approaches will arise due to the pressure coming from  
the proposed building.
Q. It is stated that the construction of the commercial 
complex  at  the  subject  premises  is  strictly  in  
accordance with the sanctioned building plan, the KMC  
Act, 1980 and the KMC Building Rules, 2009 and that the 
Corporation is strict supervising over the construction 
to ensure that no future violation or departure from  
the approved plan occurs.”
2.  We take notice of the fact that the respondent No. 8, has  
also filed an affidavit in this regard stating as under:
“ It is further stated that KMDA conducted a thorough  
analysis  of  the  pressure  bulb  for  the  proposed  
building(B+G+VI) and had also prepared a report dated  
13.12.2024 (by EE/KCD/R & B/KMDA and AE/KCD/R &B/KMDA). 
The  results  of  the  said  analysis  indicated  that  
pressure exerted from the proposed building to the  
bridge's approach wall were to be negligible. This  
analysis confirms that there is least possibility of  
harmful effect on the integrity or safety of the  
bridge- approach area' from pressure arising from the  
proposed building. True copies of the reports dated  
23.07.2024  and  13.12.2024  are  annexed  herewith  as 
Annexures R- 1 and R-2 respectively.”
3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that  
recently the State Government has taken a policy decision to stop  
the construction of all G+5 buildings in the city of Kolkata.  
According to him, the Authorities have been directed to undertake  
the necessary survey/audit/inspection of all such buildings and  
only after due approval, the construction would be permitted to be  
proceeded further.
4. We do not say anything as regards the aforesaid. If any policy  

--- Page 322 ---
decision has been taken, the Authorities will have to abide by it.  
Nothing further is required to be adjudicated in view of the  
specific stance of the KMC & KMD respectively.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

IN
 
Transfer Petition (C)   NO. 2563   OF 2025
AASHU SHARMA                                   Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
EKTA                                           Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Application for listing the review petition in open Court
is rejected.
2.  Delay condoned. 
3. The Review Petition is listed before us with an office
report on default dated 14.07.2026. The relevant portion of
the office report is as follows:
“…However,  the  Review  Petition  is
defective for the following reasons:
1. Incorrect Jurisdiction.
2. Deficit Court fees.
3.  Preamble  is  missing  in  the
petition…”
4. Despite this Registry’s letter dated 07.05.2026 to the
counsel for the petitioner to cure the defects, the defects
have not been cured so far.
5.  Even otherwise, perused  the  Review  Petition.  The  main
1

--- Page 388 ---
D.No. 20943 OF 2026
ground for the review is that the Transfer Petition is allowed
ex-parte  without giving an opportunity to the petitioner. 
6.  We have considered the matter in detail. The order dated
18.02.2026 allowing the Transfer Petition was passed on the
basis of an office report which clearly indicated that service
of notice on sole respondent is complete. Despite completion
of service the respondent has chosen not to represent himself
before the Court.
7. The Transfer Petition seeks transfer of guardianship by
Petition No. 118 of 2024 filed by the husband in Jodhpur. It
is evident from record that the child, Ishika was living with
her mother and in the natural course, a guardianship petition
should have been filed at a place where the child is living.
There is no dispute about the fact that child is living with
the mother at Bijnor. Apart from that, there are other cases
which are pending at Bijnor. 
8.  In view of the above, we are of the opinion that no case
is made out for entertaining the review petition. The review
petition is accordingly dismissed.

1

--- Page 394 ---
has already undergone 20 years of actual incarceration.
2. In  response  thereto,  the  respondent-State  of
Madhya Pradesh has filed counter affidavit. It is
stated that in addition to the present conviction,
there  are  two  other  criminal  antecedents  of  the
petitioner. It is further stated that as per the
remission policy of the State of Madhya Pradesh dated
27.05.2025, premature release of convicts, sentenced to
undergo Life Imprisonment for committing an offence
under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for
short, ‘IPC’), is excluded.
3. In such circumstances, we would have to examine
the Special Leave Petition on merit.
4. We find that petitioner has undergone total actual
period of incarceration of 20 years 11 months and 03
days without remission and more than 24 years with
remission.
5. We have also gone through the materials on record.
We are inclined to admit the appeal and grant bail to
the petitioner.
6. Leave granted.

Trial Court be called for.

before the concerned Sessions Court within a maximum
period of 07 days from today, whereafter he shall be

deemed appropriate.

ITEM NO.18               COURT NO.4               SECTION XI
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No(s).  13423/2025
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  05-12-2024
in WB No. 9423/1984 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Allahabad]
AJAY SOM & ANR.                                    Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
JAGDISH & ORS.                                     Respondent(s)
Date : 28-07-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M.M. SUNDRESH
         HON'BLE  MR. JUSTICE PRASANNA B. VARALE
For Petitioner(s) Mr. Vikash Chandra Shukla, AOR
                   Mr. Lakshya S. Pandey, Adv.
                   Ms. Isha Barshiliya, Adv.
                   Mr. Sanatan Ghosh, Adv.
                   
For Respondent(s) Mr. Pardeep Gupta, Adv.
                   Mr. Parinav Gupta, Adv.
                   Mrs. Mansi Gupta, Adv.
                   Mr. Rakshit Rathi, Adv.
                   Mr. Krishna Kumar, Adv.
                   Ms. Nandani Gupta, Adv.
                   Dr. Mrs. Vipin Gupta, AOR
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We have heard the learned counsel appearing for
the parties.
Learned  counsel  appearing  for  the  petitioners
raised two contentions.

--- Page 412 ---
2
The first contention is to the effect that there
is no registration of the adoption deed as mandated.
Secondly, the consent of the wife with respect to the
adoption has not been obtained. The High Court rightly
came to the conclusion that the recitals of the deed
itself indicated that the wife had left the deceased
several  years  ago  and  Section  16  of  the  Hindu
Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, being prospective
in nature has got no application to the deed in
question.
Furthermore, we are inclined to hold that the
issue before us is only with respect to the adoption,
and not with the transfer of property in favour of the
respondent(s).
The respondent(s) claim a right based upon the
adoption. The fact that the respondent(s) are in
possession of the subject property for a few decades
is a material fact as against the documents produced
by him before the Consolidation Officer pursuant to
the adoption.  It is significant to note that these
documents  in  support  of  the  adoption  are  public
documents.
Considering  the  above,  we  find  no  reason  to
interfere with the impugned order passed by the High
Court.
The  Special  Leave  Petition  stands  dismissed,
accordingly.

--- Page 413 ---
3
Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.
(ASHA SUNDRIYAL)                                (POONAM VAID)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                             ASSISTANT REGISTRAR

From the custody certificate dated

(8) years and thirteen (13) days. Thus as
on  date,  the  appellant  has  undergone
incarceration of more than 8 and a half

counsel for the appellant would place
before us an order passed by the Gujarat
Government,  Home  Department  dated

Subhashbhai  Champakbhai  Patel  on

Court, as affirmed by the High Court,
goes to demonstrate that the appellant
had  not  inflicted  any  blow  on  the
deceased, but has been convicted with the
aid of Section 114 IPC.
In view of the long incarceration
and abovementioned facts, we are inclined

1. Leave granted.
2. The appellant, who is the wife of the detenue, has
preferred the present appeal, being aggrieved by
the dismissal of the writ petition by the High
Court,  seeking  setting  aside  of  the  detention
order passed against the detenue. 
3. Learned counsel for the appellant raised only one
issue, as recorded by this Court while issuing
notice, that there is a clear non-application of
mind  with  respect  to  the  antecedents  of  the
appellant. While the appellant’s conviction was
modified to the offence punishable under Part II
of Section 304 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
(‘IPC’), it was noted that he was convicted under
Section 302 of the IPC.
4. While not disputing the aforesaid error, learned
counsel for the State submitted that this should
not enure to the benefit of the appellant. 
1

--- Page 457 ---
5. This is a case of clear non-application of mind.
The facts have been wrongly recorded, and the
detaining authority, if not for the same, perhaps
would not have passed the detention order.
6. Considering the above, we are inclined to set
aside the order of detention as well as the order
of the High Court.
7. The Appeal stands allowed.
8. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Shorn of facts, by order dated 10.11.2025 a Coordinate Bench
appointed a Chartered Accountant to decide on the question as to
how much amount the petitioner-borrower is liable to pay to the
respondent-Bank in accordance with the order of the Debts Recovery
Appellate  Tribunal  (DRAT)  dated  14.11.2019.  Though  the  Debts
Recovery  Tribunal  (DRT)  declined  a  counterclaim  of
Rs.30,00,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty crores), put forth as damages, the
interest payable was reduced to 6 per cent per annum simple
interest. However, the DRAT on appeal reduced the rigor and found
that in the facts and circumstances, the respondent-Bank would be
entitled for simple interest @ 9 per cent. The rejection of
counterclaim was upheld.
3. On computation, the Chartered Accountant has filed a statement
of account which as of now indicates an excess payment by the
borrower  to  the  Bank;  which  is  strongly  opposed  by  Sri  N.
Venkataraman, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents.
4. Sri N. Venkataraman, appearing for the respondent-Bank points
out that the computation is misguided and on the face of it wrong.
2

--- Page 494 ---
It is his contention that the payments made by the petitioners were
credited towards the principal and not towards the interest as is
the trite principle of law.
5. In the facts and circumstances, we are of the opinion that the
Bank should prepare a statement of accounts, with the disbursal of
loan amounts, repayments made to the loan account by the borrower,
with computation of simple interest @ 9 per cent on yearly rests
and produce the same on affidavit by the Branch Manager within a
period of two weeks from today.
6. The matters shall be listed on 13.08.2026.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioners are the husband, father-in-law and mother-in-
law of the second respondent. Marital disputes have set them apart  

--- Page 499 ---
and a child born in the wedlock is in the custody of the second  
respondent. The present special leave petition is concerned with an  
FIR registered under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and  
Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. In fact, there were  
other relatives also arrayed as accused against whom the charges  
laid have been quashed. Here the petitioners challenge an order of  
the High Court, which though quashed the complaint against two of  
the petitioners left the others to face trial.
2. We  were  of  the  opinion  that  if  there  is  an  amicable  
settlement, the dispute between the parties in its entirety can be  
sorted out. On a specific query made by us, we were told that the  
first  petitioner  is  a  Central  Government  employee  and  the  
respondent wife is unemployed, who also has the custody of child.  
We have been informed that maintenance case is pending before the  
jurisdictional Court. However, we are of the opinion that to  
facilitate a mediation, the wife and the child should be adequately  
provided for. In the circumstances subject to any orders passed by  
the  jurisdictional  Court,  we  direct  the  petitioner  to  pay  
Rs.10,000/- each to the mother and the child on a monthly basis.  
The payment shall be made before the 5th of every month starting  
from August 2026. We make it clear that the amounts fixed by us  
need  not  regulate  the  consideration  of  the  quantum  in  the  
maintenance case, which shall be fixed on the basis of the evidence  
led therein and if there is any variation in the amount, such  
variation shall be accommodated suitably from the money paid in  
accordance with our directions.
3. The parties shall be referred to the mediation, and they shall  
appear before the Mediator, online at the first instance, on  

--- Page 500 ---
10.08.2026. The physical presence of the parties shall be only as  
required by the Mediator, in which event the first petitioner shall  
be obliged to reimburse the expenses, both for, travel to and stay  
in Delhi as directed by the learned Mediator.
4. We make it clear that only the first petitioner and the second  
respondent  need  appear  before  the  Mediator,  but  the  second  
respondent can definitely be accompanied by a person, in which  
circumstance, the expenses of that person also will be borne by the  
first petitioner.
5. We post the matter on 17.08.2026

that status-quo be maintained, returnable on 28-7-2026.

Order  is  concerned,  we  find  no  error  in  the  same.  The

dwelling unit is at stake and the petitioners are ready and

adjudicated.

owe an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- and odd. There is no basis for this
particular demand made by the Bank. We reject it.
6. Since the entire amount, as directed, has been duly paid by
the petitioners, the proceedings pending before the DRT should now
be closed and the title-deeds of the property mortgaged by the
petitioners shall be handed over to the original owner of the
secured asset.

lodge it under Order XV Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
It has been brought to the notice of this court that issues
have been framed and also recasted whereunder the issue regarding
jurisdiction of the Court has been framed. Under Order XIV Rule
2(1) of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908, the Court is required to
1

--- Page 623 ---
adjudicate all the issues framed and pronounce judgment on all
issues. However, Sub-rule (2) of Rule 2 and Clause (a) of the said
sub-rule mandates that the Court should try first if that issue
relates to (a) the jurisdiction of the Court or; (b) a bar to suit
created by any law for the time being in force.
When the issue regarding jurisdiction has already been framed,
it is needless to state that said issue may be tried as a
preliminary issue and a finding be recorded on the same. 
In view of the aforesaid observation, the special leave
petition stands disposed of. 
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(DEEPANSHU)                                     (AVGV RAMU)
SENIOR PERSONAL ASSISTANT                     COURT MASTER (NSH)

ITEM NO.23               COURT NO.3               SECTION XIV
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) DIARY NO(S). 36012/2026
[ARISING OUT OF IMPUGNED FINAL JUDGMENT AND ORDER DATED  21-02-2025
IN ITA NO. 883/2019 PASSED BY THE HIGH COURT OF DELHI AT NEW DELHI]
THE COMMISSIONER OF INCOME TAX                     PETITIONER(S)
                                VERSUS
NOKIA CORPORATION                                  RESPONDENT(S)
IA NO. 179805/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING
 
Date : 17-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE B.V. NAGARATHNA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R. MAHADEVAN
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. N Venkataraman, A.S.G.
                   Mr. Sudarshan Lamba, AOR
                   Mr. Gaurav Arya, Adv.
                   Mr. Kartikay Asthana, Adv.
                   Mr. Vikash Sharma, Adv.
                   Mr. Rajendra Sahu, Adv.
Mr. V.C.Bharathi, Adv.
                   
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Ankul Goyal, Adv.
                   Ms. Tanvi Aggarwal, Adv.
                   Mr. Anmol Anand, AOR
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Learned  counsel  appearing  for  the  petitioner
submitted that in similar matters as against the very same
respondent - assessee involving the very same issues, this
Court had dismissed the Special Leave Petition on the
ground of delay and that in the instant case there is a
delay of 383 days in filing the Special Leave Petition.
Hence, appropriate orders may be made in this case also.
1

--- Page 753 ---
We find that in this case also the reasons assigned
for seeking condonation of delay are neither satisfactory
nor sufficient in law so as to condone the delay. Hence,
the application seeking condonation of delay is dismissed.
Consequently,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  is
dismissed.
We note that the petitioner was aware of the fact
that in respect of the matter as against the very same
respondents involving the very same issues, this Court had
dismissed the Special Leave Petition on the ground of gross
delay of 286 days in filing the Special Leave Petition
(Civil) Diary No.14909 of 2026. We fail to understand as to
how this Special Leave Petition could have been filed
subsequently with 383 days delay.
We further observe that the department ought to have
been conscious of the fact that Special Leave Petition
(Civil) Diary No.14909 of 2026 had been dismissed by this
Court on the ground of delay. Then, the filing of this
Special Leave Petition with a greater delay of 383 days on
the very same issue only for the sake of seeking a
dismissal on the ground of delay could have been avoided by
the Department.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
(B. LAKSHMI MANIKYA VALLI)                      (DIVYA BABBAR)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)
2

trial court in connection with FIR No. 317 of 2016 registered at
Police Station Mungwani, District Narsinghpur, Madhya Pradesh. The
conviction and sentence granted were affirmed by the High Court.
5. The  appellant,  along  with  the  co-accused  were  allegedly
apprehended with 174 kgs of Ganja in 87 packets from the trunk of
the car that they were driving. It is alleged that the accused were
in conscious possession of Ganja and were transporting the same for
sale.
6. The learned Counsel for the appellant submitted that the
appellant has been in custody since he was first arrested on
19.11.2016, i.e., for over 9 years and that both the independent
witnesses have not supported the prosecution case. Further, there
is serious infraction of Section 52A of the NDPS Act since the
sampling was done without the presence of the magistrate.
7. On a prima facie consideration, we suspend the sentence of the
appellant.
8. Appellant  shall  be  produced  before  the  Trial  Court  and
released on bail on such conditions the Trial Court may deem fit to
impose.
9. The Registry shall call for records from the Trial Court, and
soft copy of the records shall be supplied to the learned counsel
appearing for the appellant and the State.

Date : 29-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SATISH CHANDRA SHARMA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NONGMEIKAPAM KOTISWAR SINGH

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The facts of the case reveals that respondent has filed a
Civil Suit i.e. O.S. No. 699/2013 for recovery of Rs. 45,00,000/-
(Rs. Forty Five Lakh only) and petitioner/defendant was proceeded
Ex-Parte.
2. The  petitioner/defendant  after  receiving  summons  in  the
execution proceedings preferred an application under Order IX Rule
13 of Code of Civil Procedure along with an application for
condonation of delay. As there was a delay of 366 days in filing
the application under Order IX Rule 13, the District Court had

--- Page 873 ---
2
dismissed the application for condonation of delay against which an
appeal was preferred before the High Court, which was rejected by
the High Court.
3. This Court has carefully gone through the order passed by the
High Court and is of the opinion that sufficient explanation was
offered by the petitioner/defendant for condonation of delay.
4. Keeping in view the ground raised by the petitioner/defendant,
this Court is of the opinion that the application for condonation
of delay as well as the application for setting aside ex-parte
decree deserved to be allowed and they are allowed accordingly. The
suit is restored to its original number.
5. The parties shall appear before the Trial Court on 10.08.2026.
The Trial Court without being influenced by earlier orders shall be
free to pass a judgment in accordance with law.
6. The amount deposited in the Trial Court shall remain with the
Trial Court till the suit is finally decided.
7. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of accordingly.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

Court by order dated 10.02.2023 has passed the following order:
1

--- Page 897 ---
“The learned Solicitor General pointed out that the
question as to whether the power to create permanent
or sanctioned post lies in the judicial domain or not,
has been referred to a larger Bench by an order dated
07.02.2020 in  Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Vs.
Krishan Gopal & Ors.  (Civil Appeal No. 1878 of 2016)
and that the impugned order directing the creation of
the post is in the teeth of the said reference.

with Civil Appeal No. 1878 of 2016.

respondent No. 1 has now put in more than two decades
of service, his services shall not be terminated, but
he shall be continued to be engaged either in the same
post or in the equivalent cadre until further orders.”
3. It is submitted that the respondents herein also stand on the
same  footing  as  that  of  the  writ  petitioners/respondents  in
aforestated SLP.
4. In that view of the matter, we issue notice and direct that the
services of the respondent no.1 shall not be terminated and she
shall be continued to be engaged either in the same post or
equivalent cadre and all emoluments be paid, until further orders.
5. Tag with SLP (C) No.24226/2022.

ITEM NO.30                 COURT NO.3                  SECTION IV-D
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C) No(s). 568/2024
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 13-09-2023
in LPA No. 275/2023 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at
Chandigarh]
DEEPAK DOGRA                                          Petitioner(s)
             
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF PUNJAB      Respondent(s)
(IA No. 264480/2023 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED
JUDGMENT
IA No. 264481/2023 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.)
 
Date : 23-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M.M. SUNDRESH
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRASANNA B. VARALE
For Petitioner(s): Mr. Ivan Khosa, Adv.
                   Mr. Hitesh Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Tanvi Munjal, Adv.
                   Mr. Sunil Kumar Sharma, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s): Ms. Nupur Kumar, AOR
                   Mr. Rohit H Nair, Adv.
                   Ms. Muskan Surana, Adv.
                                   
Upon hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the
parties.
2. Though reliance has been placed on the judgment of
this Court in the case of Professor Ramesh Chandra v.
University of Delhi & Ors.1, in our considered view, even
in the said judgment, this Court took into consideration
1  (2015) 5 SCC 549
1

--- Page 927 ---
earlier views expressed by this Court wherein the said
principle  was applied  only  against  the  Presenting
Officer.  The Inquiry Officer is expected  to remain
impartial and submit his report on the charges levelled
against  the  delinquent  officer  by  considering  the
materials produced by the Presenting Officer vis-a-vis
the  delinquent  officer. In other words, the Inquiry
Officer does not take any s ide. Relegating him to the
position of a Presenting Officer is, therefore, not
possible. The delinquent officer should be permitted to
avail the assistance of  a legal practitioner only in
cases where the Presenting Officer is a legally trained
officer.   Notwithstanding  the  bar  contained  in  the
Policy, such assistance cannot be permitted in view of
the law laid down by this Court  to allow the petitioner
to have the assistance of a legal practitioner.
3. In  view  of  the  above,  we  are  not  inclined  to
interfere with the impugned order.
4. Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  stands
dismissed.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
 (SHUBHAM SONI)                                   (POONAM VAID)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             ASSISTANT REGISTRAR
2

Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 13001/2026

in CRM-M No. 29332/2018 passed by the High Court of Punjab &
Haryana at Chandigarh]
JASVINDER SINGH                                    Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF HARYANA & ORS.                            Respondent(s)
FOR ADMISSION 
IA No. 205815/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 
Date : 27-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UJJAL BHUYAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ATUL S. CHANDURKAR
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Yashraj Singh Deora, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Surinder Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. G C Shahpuri, Adv.
                   Mr. Arvind Gupta, AOR
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Though petitioner was initially arraigned as an accused, the
police upon conclusion of investigation, dropped him from the list
of accused. As the trial progressed, based on the evidence of PW-1
and PW-2, the informant filed application under Section 319 of the
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, ‘CrPC’) for summoning
the petitioner as an accused. It was allowed by the Trial Court in
1

--- Page 965 ---
the second round. The learned Additional Sessions Judge dismissed
the Revision Petition by observing that petitioner would be at
liberty to present his defence at an appropriate stage before the
Trial Court. When this came to be challenged before the High Court,
the High Court declined to entertain the same and rejected the
quashing petition filed vide the impugned order.
3. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner and also
perused the evidence of PW-1 and PW-3. We are of the view that no
interference is called for in the order passed by the Trial Court
under Section 319 of the CrPC summoning the petitioner as an
accused to stand trial. It would be open to the petitioner to avail
all possible pleas and grounds of defence in the course of the
trial.
4. Subject to the above, Special Leave Petition is dismissed.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
 (IRAMNAZ)                                       (CHETNA BALOONI)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)

Heard.
Delay condoned.
The grievance of the petitioner is that he had been appointed
under the disability quota based on the certificate produced by him
which assessed his disability at 60 per cent and as per the
Advertisement dated 18.05.2022 the minimum disability ought to be
1

--- Page 1007 ---
40 per cent. Hence, the petitioner was appointed.
Respondent(s)-employer  on  clinical  examination  of  the
petitioner found that he had only 30 per cent disability or in
other  words  he  did  not  possess  the  requisite  percentage  of
disability for being appointed namely 40 per cent disability.
Hence, his services came to be terminated on 19.11.2025 which
was challenged before the High Court in Civil Writ Petition No.
19015/2025. During the pendency of the said writ petition, a report
was called for from the  All India Institute of Medical Sciences
(“for short  AIIMS”), Jodhpur and for which a Medical Board was
constituted by the said hospital as evident from Annexure P-13.
It is the grievance of the petitioner that even before the
report of the AIIMS, Jodhpur could be examined by the High Court
which was also noticed by the High Court viz., report not having
received, yet proceeded to paint the said petitioner in the same
category of other candidates who did not possess the requisite
qualification and thereby dismissed his Writ Petition enormously. 
Hence, for the limited purpose of ascertaining as to whether
the High Court had sufficient material including the report of
AIIMS, Jodphur prior to passing the impugned order, we issue notice
to the respondents, returnable in four weeks.
(DEEPANSHU)                                     (AVGV RAMU)
